Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

The buyer is Wattlebridge Holdings, acquisition of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures. The seller's draft SPA has many positions departing from the buyer's playbook. Let me go through each area systematically.

Let me review each position against the buyer's playbook:

1. **General warranty cap: 20% / AUD 4,800,000**
   - Buyer: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000; 20% cap only with Amelia Frost written authority (none given). No conditional fallback without explicit prior written approval.
   - Seller offers unconditional 20% / AUD 4,800,000. This needs pushback — needs to revert to 25% or require Amelia's authority.
   - **Material issue.** Departure: unconditional below-position cap. Need to demand either revert to 25% / AUD 6M, or obtain Amelia's written approval for the 20% cap with specified conditions. If no compromise, buyer can refuse the deal entirely and walk.

2. **Thresholds: de minimis AUD 25,000, basket AUD 250,000**
   - Buyer: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from first dollar once exceeded.
   - Seller proposes tighter thresholds (25K/250K). Below this is an unactionable slab. This is a tiny amount — let's compute: 4,800,000 × 20% = 960,000 cap. So the de minimis only matters if a claim exceeds... hmm. Actually the cap is the total max liability. De minimis excludes trivial claims before aggregation kicks in. 25K threshold is only relevant if there are multiple small claims that add up below basket. Given aggregate 250K, anything under 250K is non-actionable (first 25K exempt, then 250K exempt, remainder recoverable). For a 100% sale at 24M, these thresholds are negligible compared to the 4.8M cap. But they're still below our $5K/$50K benchmark. The bigger issue is the combined effect: effectively very low thresholds. But again, impact on liability cap is minimal — once a claim hits say $300K it's recoverable. It mainly matters for granular claims distribution. I'd recommend negotiating at least 25K de minimis and 50K basket (i.e., bring back to buyer positions) or at minimum a mutual agreed position. Actually since 250K > 50K, bringing up to 50K/50K achieves "seller liable from first dollar" which matches playbook — except "from first dollar" vs "exceeding basket". Our playbook says seller liable from first dollar once exceeded (meaning first dollar above de minimis of 5K and above 50K? Actually typical basket clauses work as: below de minimis not actionable; between de minimis and basket excluded; above basket only excess recoverable). The phrase "aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded" suggests once a claim exceeds the 50K basket, the entire claim (or all amounts above basket) are recoverable. Actually there are two styles: "above basket only excess" vs "above basket, full recovery". Playbook says "seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded" = any dollar above the basket is recoverable (full amount, not just excess). That's simpler/more buyer-friendly. I'll note this and recommend alignment.

   **Recommendation**: Raise de minimis to AUD 5,000 and basket to AUD 50,000 (matching playbook), with full-amount recovery once exceeding both thresholds. Or accept and push only minimal margin up. Let's recommend raising to at least match playbook; meaningful improvement if we raise basket substantially.

3. **Time limits: 18 months general Warranty**
   - Buyer: 24 months baseline; 18 months is fallback needing Amelia written approval (none given).
   - Seller proposes 18 months unconditionally. This is a direct material departure.
   - **Material issue.** Demand revert to 24 months. If seller insists 18 months, reject unless Amelia Frost gives unconditional written approval with specific identification of the draft.

4. **Fundamental/Title: same caps and time limits as general warranties**
   - Buyer: fundamental/title claims separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
   - Seller collapses title/capacity into general regime.
   - **Material issue.** This could be substantively justified as administrative simplicity but materially weakens title protection. If we allow it, all title claims fall within 4.8M cap + 18 months, with no six-year lookback and outside the knowledge bar. Pushback required: maintain independent title warranty regime with 100% cap, 6-year lookback, standalone time limit, outside the general cap structure. Require separate clause drafting.

5. **Limitations/reliance: applies to ALL Claims of any nature**
   - Buyer: fraud, wilful concealment carve-out "to the maximum extent enforceable" and no one may waive.
   - Seller: limitations apply to all claims. No explicit fraud carve-out. Could be read as inconsistent if paired with their own fraud carve-out elsewhere, but as stated it's unfavorable.
   - **Material issue**. Add explicit carve-out: fraud, wilful/gross negligence concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum extent enforceable regardless of limitation/exclusivity/non-reliance provisions. Confirm no Seller-side waiver. Note typical Australian law has 'fraudulent claims' dealt with in PFMA generally; this matters.

6. **Disclosure: rely on general disclosure, data room + public registers**
   - Buyer: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room/public-register deemed disclosure.
   - Seller relies on general blanket disclosure.
   - **Material issue.** Reject as drafted. Demand Schedule 7 with specific itemized disclosure (DD-002 through DD-012). Require distinct treatment of each DD item, not bundled general disclosure. Reject "without limiting any specific disclosure below."

7. **Clause 8.3 buyer knowledge: no claim in respect of knowledge of matter**
   - Buyer: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud, specific indemnity.
   - Seller Clause 8.3 is a blanket exclusion of buyer knowledge. Exactly opposite of playbook.
   - **Material issue.** This clause is a core red flag. Delete entirely or replace with narrow formulation: identify specific knowledge persons with name and role, require reasonable enquiry process, exclude only valid defenses known or reasonably knowable at reasonable diligence — never excusing title, capacity, fraud, or a specific indemnity.

8. **Bluefen change-control consent: reasonable endeavours / consent satisfied on delivery**
   - Buyer: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient for material customer consent.
   - Seller uses reasonable endeavours, treats consent satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent. No evidence provided.
   - **Material issue.** Demand written Bluefen consent included in SPA before Completion AND confirmation that 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Treat "reasonable endeavours" inadequate.

9. **Riverlark: post-completion release**
   - Buyer: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; post-completion release needs irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
   - Seller proposes release after Completion (no undertaking).
   - **Material issue.** Demand current redemption (Completion day) plus repayment directly from Completion funds; if release needed later, include irrevocable undertakings + Amelia Frost approval. Propose immediate discharge if possible.

10. **DD-005 Employee bonuses: AUD 420,000 not itemized, funds flow silent**
    - Buyer: must be specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
    - Seller acknowledges but says "matter for the Seller" and not itemized.
    - **Material issue.** Force-add a specific line item AUD 420,000 + on-costs into completion funds flow explicitly. Require seller to confirm payment terms (cash vs accrued, super/tax treatment) or provide letter. Don't permit silent omission.

11. **Ironquay IP: limited to SOW3 payment**
    - Buyer: broaden narrow indemnity, preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way.
    - Seller: adequate as-is.
    - **Material issue.** Don't accept. Broaden scope, add condition that AUD 180,000 remains open and clearly broken out in pricing; preserve SOW3 cure mechanisms; require payment receipt or assignment documents. Flag to buyer principal.

12. **Export/privacy (DD-006): preliminary, not material**
    - Buyer: preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand.
    - Seller: not material.
    - Material issue: buyer instruction explicitly to assume no confirmed breach — don't settle at "preliminary operational matter." Demand preserving logs, ongoing investigation, updates, no premature minimization characterization. Also note 1,240 records exposed — even pre-breach, privacy exposure exists. This may be separable issue but buyer wants no confirmed breach assumption.

13. **Office lease (DD-007): obligation described as notification obligation but not landlord consent requirement**
    - Buyer: no automatic debt classification or price deduction for ordinary-course costs.
    - Seller: notes a notification obligation identified, but doesn't describe it as requiring landlord consent.
    - This is relatively minor but worth confirming whether lease transfer is seamless; if so no Seller obligation beyond notification. Don't classify as debt/price deduction; confirm no landlord consent gap leaks into personal service provisions. Minor issue.

14. **Supplier renewals (AUD 330,000): ordinary course**
    - Buyer: assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
    - Seller: three renewals AUD 110K each ordinary-course operating costs, no classification flagged.
    - Material issue: need to verify each renewal's trigger/force majeure status; ordinary course exemption requires evidence. AUD 330K at ~14% of price is moderate; worth confirming each individually isn't a renewal triggered by sale but normal rate adjustment. Assess all three, confirm ordinary course per business-as-usual definition. Possibly raise to risk-free characterization if needed. Accept without classification but verify.

15. **Tax/IP: settled under general regime**
    - Buyer: Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
    - Seller settles under general cap.
    - **Material issue.** Buyer says tax/IP remain OPEN. Don't accept "settled under general regime." Keep Title/Tax/IP separate, no hidden general-regime override. Demand explicit tax/IP warranty commitments with capped amounts, separate baskets where appropriate.

16. **Title: DD-012 share register, not independent verification**
    - Buyer: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is supplied internal source, not independent proof.
    - Seller relies on DD-012 register.
    - **Material issue.** Don't accept reliance on internal register without external corroboration. Require independent title searches, statutory filings, share certificates or custodial evidence of share ownership, and encumbrance check across all JV/partner entities. Request outside counsel confirming title clean.

17. **Clause-specific / consistency checks:**
    - No hidden general-regime override hiding Title/Tax/IP inside general cap structure.
    - Need to ensure Title, Tax, IP, Payment, Covenant categories kept separate; no buried general regime.
    - Also: Clause 12.3 "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" — good on caps fallback but conflicts with fundamental/title separate regime discussed. Need harmonization.

Additional structural issues:
- **Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark)**: "address by release following Completion" — issue.
- **Clause 12.1/12.2**: caps thresholds low; already noted.
- General 24-month period? They have 12.3 saying 18 months; no general 24-month clause to override.
- Fraud/wilful carve-out likely present in Seller's reference only? Document says "to maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this" in playbook; seller doesn't mention it in summary. If absent, we should insist inclusion.

Also note: Settlement clauses — should ask whether completion fund payment includes DD-005 paid/deferred.

Let me now write my recommendations in structured format:
- Identify departures: grouped by topic with issue number, conclusion, buyer action, reasoning.
- Then executive recommendation summary.

I need to be concise but complete. Let me craft the response with ~6-8 substantive items flagged as major issues, possibly 2 minor/verification items. Then a recommendation bullet list.

Structure:
1. Summary at top briefly.
2. Departures table or numbered list of key issues, each with: Issue → Seller Position → Buyer Position → Recommendation & Reasoning.
3. Bottom-line recommendations prioritized.

Let me draft.

Key major issues to flag:
- (A) General Warranty cap: unconditional 20%/AUD4.8M below position. Must revert to 25%/AUD6M or secured Amelia written authority; otherwise walk. Reasoning: no authority granted; position would cap buyer warranty rights at 4.8M with seller-favored thresholds and no rest.
- (B) Thresholds: 25K/250K. Bring to 5K/50K matching playbook; rationalize effect. Even modest tightening reduces actionable triggers; we want 50K basket with "seller liable from first dollar above both bars". Reason: aligns with playbook; lowers seller-favorable thresholds.
- (C) Time limit 18 months vs 24 month baseline. Unconditional. Must revert to 24 months, or Amelia must approve 18-month fallback with specified draft identification and conditions. Reason: core warranty window, matters for discoverable defects.
- (D) Fundamental/Title collapsed into general regime: separate regime required — 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside general caps/de minimis/knowledge. Reason: capacity & title claims often significant; generic caps undervalue.
- (E) Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion (Clause 8.3). Delete or rewrite to strict named-person + reasonable-enquiry standard excluding title/capacity/fraud/specific indemnities. Reason: playbook deletes such exclusions; blanket exclusions are a seller-concession trap.
- (F) Disclosure schedule treats data room/public registers as sufficient. Replace with Itemised Schedule 7 — one DD item per disclosure, no "without limiting" boilerplate. Reason: our disclosure policy rejects deemed/general disclosure.
- (G) Bluefen: reasonable endeavours insufficient. Require effective written consent before Completion + evidence conditions satisfied; no consent-on-delivery. Reason: 30% of FY26 revenue; material customer change-control.
- (H) Riverlark release post-Completion lacking undertake. Demand immediate redemption + repayment from Completion funds; if late release needed, irrevocable undertaking + Amelia approval. Reason: Separation of risk; early discharge preferred.
- (I) DD-005 bonuses silent in funds flow. Force-add AUD 420k line; define payment/on-costs treatment; no silent omission. Reason: buyer requires specific funding stream.
- (J) Ironquay IP: keep open; broaden indemnity, preserve SOW3 cure, flag 180K. Reason: playbook opens tax/IP; value unlikely to clear standalone cap without additional commercial transaction.
- (K) Export incident: characterization "not material" conflicts with preserve-logs/investigate instruction; preserve 1,240 records exposure, no confirmed breach assumption beyond buyer instruction — treat as open disclosure item. Reason: buyer explicitly instructs assuming no breach but also requires investigation + logs preserved.
- (L) Supplier renewals: verify ordinary-course, no forced classification. Reason: 330K; need diligence on whether any renewal is sale-triggered. If renewal avoided, don't classify.
- (M) Title: internal register alone insufficient. Require independent title search, certificate evidence, encumbrance report, custodian confirmation. Reason: DD-012 not independent evidence.
- (N) Tax/IP "settled under general regime": contradicted by buyer open positions; retain separate. Reason: closing principle contradicts open.
- (O) Fraud carve-out missing or general; ensure presence; no waiver. Reason: playbook mandates carve-out to maximum; vague general limitation defeats.
- (P) Office lease DD-007: confirm no landlord consent gap across jurisdictions; avoid treating as debt. Minor verification.

Now synthesize recommendations:
1. Cannot close this draft as-is on several points. Tell seller specifically which clause demands change, what each changes to. Give priority list: cap/time/fundamental, knowledge clause, Bluefen, Riverlark, DD-005, Title. These are immovable positions; negotiable if Seller willing — confirm.
